detailed_rationale:
IRCON International is a Ministry of Railways EPC PSU executing railway, highway and other infrastructure projects domestically and overseas. FY26 operating revenue came in around Rs 9,071-10,760cr depending on the source/consolidation basis, which is a genuine decline versus prior years - matching the quant feed's -15.7% one-year and -4.4% three-year revenue trend, among the weaker growth readings in this batch (growth_1y_score just 3.0, growth_3y_score 5.0). Notably, Q4 FY26 PAT of ~Rs 191.5cr held up reasonably (one headline explicitly frames it as 'Profit at Rs 192 Crore... Amid Revenue Dip'), suggesting margins or other income partly cushioned the topline decline rather than profit collapsing in step with revenue - a modest positive, though not one we can fully attribute without more granular disclosure.

The order book stood at Rs 24,984cr as of FY26-end (Rs 19,459cr railways, Rs 3,919cr highways, Rs 1,606cr other), split 54% competitive-bid and 46% nomination-basis (i.e., directly awarded by Indian Railways/government without tender - typically lower execution risk but not necessarily higher margin). At roughly 2.3-2.8x trailing revenue, this order book provides reasonable but not exceptional multi-year visibility - meaningfully thinner cover than some peers in this batch (e.g., NCC's order book runs closer to 4x revenue). There is no clear evidence in what we found of a specific catalyst (new mega-award, cost turnaround, or balance-sheet repair) that would explain why the current revenue decline should reverse sharply from here; this reads as a genuine, if unremarkable, execution slowdown for a railway-EPC PSU rather than a company in acute distress (D/E 0.86, interest coverage 2.19x are unremarkable but not alarming) or one with an identified imminent turn.
recommendation_rationale: Revenue is genuinely declining, growth scores are among the weakest in this batch, and while the order book offers some multi-year visibility, it is not large enough relative to current revenue to be a strong conviction case for an imminent re-acceleration. Profit held up better than revenue in the most recent quarter, which is a mild positive, but not enough on its own - absent a specific catalyst - to override the quant Sell.
summary: IRCON's revenue has been declining for the past year even as profit held up somewhat better, and while its railway-project order book offers reasonable visibility, it is not large enough relative to current revenue to strongly signal an imminent turnaround. We recommend Sell.
positive_para: IRCON carries a reasonable order book (Rs 24,984cr, ~78% railways) with more than half won through competitive bidding, and Q4 FY26 profit of ~Rs 192cr held up better than the topline decline would suggest, hinting at some margin resilience. As a Ministry of Railways PSU, it also benefits from a steady pipeline of government rail-infrastructure spending.
negative_para: Revenue has genuinely declined for two consecutive readings (-15.7% one-year, -4.4% three-year CAGR), and growth scores are among the weakest in this batch. The order book, while reasonable, covers only a little over two years of revenue at the current run-rate - not the kind of multi-year backlog cushion that would strongly argue for a near-term reacceleration - and nearly half of it is nomination-based awards, which typically carry government-set rather than market-tested margins.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~20.6x trailing earnings, the multiple is undemanding in absolute terms, but it is being paid for a business with a currently shrinking topline and only moderate order-book cover - fair compensation for the uncertainty rather than a clear bargain. Judgment: fair.
